First, we recall the sum formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u+v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v-\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the sum formula for cosine with $u=x$ and $v=\frac{5\pi }{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+\frac{5\pi }{6}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6})-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
